intentAndPurpose.intent: Mutually exclusive segmented control for switching between related views or filters. Wraps Base UI ToggleGroup. Supports track emphasis, attention-driven selected states, equal-width layout, text and icon-only segments, and start (icon) / end (CounterBadge) slots.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent colour role for active segments at high and medium attention. Omitted or `auto` resolves to `primary`, matching the Figma default. At `low` attention the selected segment follows the track/background role (parent Surface appearance, or neutral at page root) instead.

props.name: attention
props.description: Drives the SELECTED segment fill prominence. Default: `high`.

props.name: equalWidth
props.description: Equal-width segments. Default depends on `type`: text → `true` (fill track); icon → `false` (fixed square cells). Figma API describes distributing equal width regardless of content length.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the selected segment changes

props.name: type
props.description: `text` (default) or `icon` — icon-only requires `aria-label` on each item.

interactionBehavior.summary: SegmentedControl is a required single-select ToggleGroup whose selected fill is a sliding pill behind the segments, not a background on the item. Unselected hover is a second pill that follows the cursor in JS; selected hover/press tint that same active pill via `:has()`, so there is never a second fill racing the glide. Arrow keys move focus only — `Enter` / `Space` / click commit — and the currently selected segment cannot be turned off.
hover: Unselected hover does not paint the item: a `.hoverIndicator` pill glides to the hovered segment in `--{TrackRole}-Subtle` at `trackEmphasis="high"`, or `--{TrackRole}-Minimal` at medium/low. The item only keeps `--{TrackRole}-High` text.
The pill is driven by `pointermove` on the group. `pointerType === "touch"` is ignored, and the pill hides when the pointer is over a disabled or already-selected (`[data-pressed]`) segment.

Selected hover tints the `.activeIndicator` itself via `:has(.item[data-pressed]:hover)`: `--{Role}-Bold-Hover` at `attention="high"`, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` at medium, `--{Role}-Subtle-Hover` of the track role at low.
Both hover fills are wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover pill.
press: An unselected press fills the item's state-layer with the track pressed token (`--{TrackRole}-Subtle-Pressed` at high track emphasis, `--{TrackRole}-Pressed` at medium/low) — this is fill-on-the-item, not the hover pill, and is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded.
A selected press tints the active pill via `:has(.item[data-pressed]:active)` to `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed` / `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` / track `--{Role}-Subtle-Pressed` by attention.
There is no tap-scale on the segment. Feedback is pill + text colour only.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the inner state-layer: `--Stroke-XL` gap in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring.
A high-attention selected segment prepends `--Elevation-1` to that same `box-shadow` so the raised pill and the halo coexist.
`:focus` only clears the native outline; the ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click does not paint it.
keyboard: Each segment is a native `<button aria-pressed>`. `Enter` / `Space` select it; they do not live in OneUI code — Base UI Toggle + `useButton` handle them.
`ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` move focus only. They do not change the selected segment. `Home` / `End` jump focus to the first / last enabled segment. `loopFocus` is always on.
Disabled segments are natively `disabled`, so arrows skip them.
Clicking or key-activating the already-selected segment would toggle it off in Base UI, but the group's `onValueChange` ignores an empty array, so selection is required — the pill never disappears.
selected: Selected is Base UI Toggle `pressed`, exposed as `aria-pressed` and `[data-pressed]`. The fill lives on `.activeIndicator`, not on the item — the item's state-layer only changes text colour.

`attention="high"`: pill is `--{Role}-Bold` (or `--{Role}-Material-Fill` when the role has a material) plus `--Elevation-1`, text `--{Role}-Bold-High`. Medium: `--{Role}-Subtle` fill, `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text. Low: track-role `--{Role}-Subtle` fill, track `--{Role}-TintedA11y` text.

On a selection change `.activeIndicator` glides to the new segment: `transform: translateX(...)` plus a `width` transition over `--Motion-Duration-L` / `--Motion-Easing-Transition-Moderate`. It only eases while continuously visible; a pill appearing fresh (through `display` + `allow-discrete`) fades in at the target spot instead of sliding from a stale position.
The one place motion is intentionally killed is resize — the pill is repositioned with `transition: none` for a single frame so a window resize never replays the tap-to-select glide.
disabled: A disabled group sets `[data-disabled]` and dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` with `cursor: not-allowed`. A per-item `disabled` is a native `disabled` attribute plus `pointer-events: none`.

Because the item is natively disabled with `pointer-events: none`, `cursor: not-allowed` on the item is not observable — the pointer shows the group's cursor. This is the known system-wide gap (docs/design/disabled-states.md).
Hover pill tracking skips `[data-disabled]` items, and every hover/press selector excludes them.
touch: Touch pointers never drive the hover pill (`pointerType === "touch"` returns before measuring), so a tap does not leave a hover fill on the next segment.
The pressed fill on an unselected segment, then the active pill glide, are the entire tap response.
